core_obligations: Show that the restriction of a finite length R-module along the local homomorphism has the same finite length l over R' (proof lines 16450-16452).

Observe that an admissible sequence x_1, ..., x_l of M over R remains admissible over R' because m' maps into m, so that the same tuple of symbols can be compared in the two determinant modules (proof lines 16453-16455).

Define the isomorphism by sending [x_1, ..., x_l] in det_{R,kappa}(M) to the corresponding symbol in det_{R',kappa}(M), and verify that it is functorial for isomorphisms and compatible with the isomorphisms gamma of the additivity lemma (proof lines 16456-16462).
proof_roadmap: Length preservation along the local homomorphism (proof lines 16450-16452).
Inheritance of admissibility and the symbol-wise definition of the isomorphism (proof lines 16453-16459).
Functoriality and compatibility with gamma (proof lines 16460-16462).
difficulty_reason: For a local homomorphism of local rings (R', m') -> (R, m) inducing an isomorphism on residue fields, the lemma asserts that the restriction M_{R'} of a finite length R-module is again of finite length and that there is a canonical isomorphism det_{R,kappa}(M) -> det_{R',kappa}(M_{R'}), functorial in M and compatible with the isomorphism gamma of the additivity lemma for short exact sequences (statement lines 16433-16447). The proof has three parts: the length is preserved, by the algebra lemma on pushdown of a module of finite length; an admissible sequence over R is again admissible over R' because m' maps into m, which is what makes the symbol comparison possible; and the isomorphism is defined by sending the symbol [x_1, ..., x_l] in det_{R,kappa}(M) to the corresponding symbol in det_{R',kappa}(M), after which functoriality and compatibility with gamma are immediate to verify (proof lines 16450-16462). Observing that admissibility is inherited along the map on maximal ideals, which is what makes the symbol-wise definition legitimate, is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2.
